D: Newt Scamander goes to Paris to find Credence while Grindelwald gathers followers.
P: Serve the snacks when Newt and Jacob arrive in Paris.
S: Newt and Jacob arriving in Paris
Puff pastry triangles rolled around a stick of dark chocolate, egg washed and baked at 200C for 15 minutes.
Yeasted doughnuts fried at 175C until golden, filled with plum jam and dusted with icing sugar.

Crisp golden choux puffs beaten with gruyère, nutmeg and black pepper, baked until hollow and served warm in a napkin-lined basket. Bring 125ml water, 125ml milk, 100g butter and a pinch of salt to the boil. Tip in 150g plain flour and beat over the heat for 2 minutes until the dough comes away from the sides. Cool 5 minutes, then beat in 4 eggs one at a time until glossy. Stir in 120g grated gruyère, a pinch of nutmeg and pepper. Pipe walnut-size balls onto lined trays, top with a little more cheese and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden.
M: Paris in 1927, the night of the rally

Chicken braised in red wine with bacon lardons, mushrooms, little onions and thyme until tender, spooned over buttery mash. Brown 1.2kg chicken pieces and 150g bacon lardons. Add 12 small onions and 250g mushrooms, then 500ml red wine, 250ml stock and thyme. Simmer covered 45 minutes and serve with 800g potatoes mashed with butter.
Hogwarts staff room chicken leek pie

Chicken and leek pie in a creamy sauce under puff pastry, baked at 200C for 25 minutes. Brown 800g diced chicken thigh in 30g butter and set aside. Soften 2 sliced leeks in the same pan, stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 300ml chicken stock and 150ml cream and simmer until thick. Add the chicken, chopped thyme and a spoon of Dijon and season. Spoon into a pie dish, cover with 1 sheet puff pastry, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden. Serve with buttered peas.
W: Queenie and her magic in the kitchen
Apples, sultanas, cinnamon and breadcrumbs rolled in buttered filo, baked at 190C for 35 minutes until crisp, dusted with icing sugar.
K: Paris café au lait with vanilla Chantilly

Strong coffee and steaming milk poured together into big bowl-sized cups, topped with vanilla whipped cream and a dusting of cocoa. Whip 150ml cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar and half a teaspoon vanilla to soft peaks. Brew 500ml strong coffee in a plunger or stovetop pot. Heat 500ml full cream milk until steaming and froth it with a whisk. Pour the coffee and milk into 4 big cups at the same time, half and half. Top with a spoon of the vanilla cream and a pinch of cocoa.

s.note: Newt and Jacob arriving in Paris
s.how: Cut 2 puff pastry sheets into long triangles. Lay a stick of dark chocolate at the wide end and roll up towards the point. Curve into crescents, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until puffed and golden.

Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast, 2 eggs, 50g butter and warm milk into a soft dough and prove an hour. Roll into balls, prove again and fry at 175C until golden. Pipe plum jam into each and dust with icing sugar. A proper bakery treat.

m.note: Paris in 1927, the night of the rally
m.how: Brown 1.2kg chicken pieces and 150g bacon lardons. Add 12 small onions and 250g mushrooms, then 500ml red wine, 250ml stock and thyme. Simmer covered 45 minutes and serve with 800g potatoes mashed with butter.

w.note: Queenie and her magic in the kitchen
w.how: Toss 4 sliced green apples with 80g sultanas, a teaspoon of cinnamon and a handful of breadcrumbs. Layer buttered filo sheets, spread the filling along one edge and roll up. Brush with butter and bake at 190C for 35 minutes. Dust with icing sugar.
